benchmarks.name: MMLU-Pro
benchmarks.blurb: 12,000 reasoning-heavy multiple-choice questions across 14 academic subjects, with ten options instead of four. The harder successor to MMLU.

benchmarks.name: GPQA Diamond
benchmarks.blurb: 198 graduate-level physics, chemistry and biology questions written to be Google-proof. PhD holders in the matching field score about 65%.

benchmarks.name: AIME 2025
benchmarks.blurb: The American Invitational Mathematics Examination — 15 problems, integer answers, no partial credit. A standard test of multi-step maths reasoning.

benchmarks.name: MATH-500
benchmarks.blurb: 500 competition maths problems sampled from the MATH benchmark, graded on the final answer.

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Verified
benchmarks.blurb: 500 human-validated GitHub issues from real Python repositories. The model must produce a patch that makes the project's own tests pass.

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Pro
benchmarks.blurb: A harder, contamination-resistant successor to SWE-bench Verified, drawn from commercial and copyleft repositories that were never public training data.

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 2.1
benchmarks.blurb: The 2.1 revision of the terminal agent benchmark. Scores on it are not comparable with Terminal-Bench 4.0 — the task set changed.

benchmarks.name: Frontier-Bench v0.1
benchmarks.blurb: Novel problems built to resist memorisation, scored on whether the model gets anywhere at all. Absolute numbers are low by design.

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 4.0
benchmarks.blurb: End-to-end tasks in a real terminal — install, build, debug, run — scored on whether the machine ends up in the required state.

benchmarks.name: LiveCodeBench
benchmarks.blurb: Competitive-programming problems collected after each model's training cutoff, so contamination cannot inflate the score.

benchmarks.name: HumanEval
benchmarks.blurb: 164 short Python functions written from a docstring. Saturated at the frontier — kept here for continuity with older models.

benchmarks.name: MMMU
benchmarks.blurb: College-level questions that require reading charts, diagrams, tables and photographs alongside the text.

benchmarks.name: IFEval
benchmarks.blurb: Verifiable instructions — word counts, formats, forbidden words — checked by a program rather than a judge model.

benchmarks.name: LMArena Elo
benchmarks.blurb: Elo rating from blind pairwise votes by the public on LMArena. Measures what people prefer, not what is correct.

models.name: GPT-5
models.desc: OpenAI's flagship reasoning model, with an adjustable thinking budget that routes easy prompts to a fast path and hard ones to extended reasoning.

models.name: GPT-5 mini
models.desc: A cheaper GPT-5 tuned for well-defined tasks — the default choice when the prompt is clear and the volume is high.

models.name: GPT-5 nano
models.desc: The smallest GPT-5, priced for classification, extraction and routing rather than open-ended reasoning.

models.name: o3
models.desc: The reasoning model that preceded GPT-5, and the first to use tools inside its own chain of thought.

models.name: o4-mini
models.desc: A small reasoning model that punches far above its price on maths and code.

models.name: o3-mini
models.desc: The first cheap reasoning model, with selectable low/medium/high effort.

models.name: o1
models.desc: The model that introduced inference-time reasoning to a mainstream API.

models.name: GPT-4.1
models.desc: A million-token non-reasoning model built for long-context retrieval and instruction following.

models.name: GPT-4.1 mini
models.desc: Most of GPT-4.1's behaviour at a fifth of the price, same million-token window.

models.name: GPT-4.1 nano
models.desc: OpenAI's cheapest million-token model — autocomplete, tagging and routing.

models.name: GPT-4o
models.desc: The natively multimodal model that set the price floor for frontier chat in 2024.

models.name: GPT-4o mini
models.desc: For two years the default cheap model for high-volume production work.

models.name: gpt-oss-120b
models.desc: OpenAI's first open-weight release since GPT-2 — a sparse mixture of experts that fits on a single 80GB accelerator.

models.name: gpt-oss-20b
models.desc: The small open-weight sibling — designed to run on a 16GB consumer GPU.

models.name: Claude Opus 4.5
models.desc: Anthropic's most capable model, and the first Opus priced within reach of everyday production use.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.5
models.desc: The workhorse of the Claude 4.5 family — strongest of its generation at long-running agentic coding, with a million-token window in beta.

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.desc: Near-Sonnet-4 coding ability at a third of the price and roughly twice the speed.

models.name: Claude Opus 4.1
models.desc: An incremental upgrade to Opus 4 focused on multi-file refactoring accuracy.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4
models.desc: The first Claude with a hybrid instant/extended-thinking switch in the API.

models.name: Claude 3.7 Sonnet
models.desc: The bridge release that introduced visible extended thinking to Claude.

models.name: Claude 3.5 Sonnet
models.desc: The 2024 coding benchmark other labs measured themselves against.

models.name: Claude 3.5 Haiku
models.desc: A fast, cheap Claude that matched the previous generation's flagship on code.

models.name: Claude 3 Opus
models.desc: The first Claude to trade blows with GPT-4, and still prized for prose.

models.name: Gemini 3 Pro
models.desc: Google's frontier model — a million-token window that natively ingests video and audio, not just text and stills.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.desc: The first Gemini with reasoning on by default, and a long run at the top of the public preference leaderboards.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
models.desc: A thinking model with a budget dial you set per request — including zero.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite
models.desc: Google's cheapest million-token model, aimed at classification and summarisation.

models.name: Gemini 2.0 Flash
models.desc: The generation that made million-token context ordinary rather than premium.

models.name: Gemini 1.5 Pro
models.desc: The two-million-token model that proved long context could work in production.

models.name: Gemma 3 27B
models.desc: Google's open-weight flagship — multimodal, 140 languages, one GPU.

models.name: Gemma 3 12B
models.desc: The mid-size Gemma 3 — the usual pick for a 24GB card.

models.name: Gemma 3 4B
models.desc: Small enough for a laptop, still multimodal and 128k-context.

models.name: Llama 4 Maverick
models.desc: 128 experts, 17B active — Meta's first natively multimodal open-weight model.

models.name: Llama 4 Scout
models.desc: A ten-million-token context window — the longest ever shipped in open weights.

models.name: Llama 3.3 70B
models.desc: 405B-class quality distilled into 70B — for a year, the open-weight default.

models.name: Llama 3.1 405B
models.desc: The release that first put a genuinely frontier-class model into open weights.

models.name: Llama 3.1 8B
models.desc: The most fine-tuned open model in existence, and the standard small baseline.

models.name: Llama 3.2 90B Vision
models.desc: Meta's first open vision-language model at scale.

models.name: Llama 3.2 3B
models.desc: Built for phones and edge devices, with tool calling intact.

models.name: Mistral Medium 3
models.desc: Mistral's price-performance flagship, aimed squarely at enterprise deployment.

models.name: Mistral Large 2
models.desc: The 123B dense model that anchored Mistral's line for two years.

models.name: Magistral Medium
models.desc: Mistral's first reasoning model, with traces in the user's own language.

models.name: Magistral Small
models.desc: Open-weight reasoning at 24B — runs on a single 32GB card.

models.name: Mistral Small 3.2 24B
models.desc: The best-regarded Apache-2.0 model in the 24B class, and multimodal.

models.name: Devstral Medium
models.desc: A coding agent model trained on repository-scale edit trajectories.

models.name: Codestral 25.08
models.desc: Mistral's fill-in-the-middle code model, built for editor autocomplete.

models.name: Ministral 8B
models.desc: An edge model with sliding-window attention for cheap long context.

models.name: Mixtral 8x22B
models.desc: The sparse mixture of experts that popularised the architecture in open weights.

models.name: Pixtral Large
models.desc: A 124B multimodal model with a 1B vision encoder bolted to Mistral Large.

models.name: DeepSeek-V3.2
models.desc: Introduced DeepSeek Sparse Attention, cutting long-context cost by roughly half at equal quality.

models.name: DeepSeek-V3.1
models.desc: A single set of weights that switches between thinking and non-thinking modes.

models.name: DeepSeek-R1
models.desc: The open-weight reasoning model that showed pure reinforcement learning could produce chain-of-thought without supervised traces.

models.name: DeepSeek-V3
models.desc: Trained for a reported $5.6M in GPU time — the release that reset assumptions about what frontier training has to cost.

models.name: Qwen3-Max
models.desc: Alibaba's largest model, and the first Qwen kept closed.

models.name: Qwen3-235B-A22B
models.desc: Apache-2.0 frontier weights with a hybrid thinking switch and 119 languages.

models.name: Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B
models.desc: The strongest open-weight agentic coding model of its generation, with a native 256k window extensible to a million.

models.name: Qwen3-32B
models.desc: A dense 32B with the same thinking switch as its much larger siblings.

models.name: Qwen3-30B-A3B
models.desc: Only 3B parameters active per token — the fastest way to run a capable open model on modest hardware.

models.name: QwQ-32B
models.desc: A 32B reasoning model that traded blows with 671B models on maths.

models.name: Qwen2.5-72B
models.desc: The dense 72B that made Qwen a default choice outside China.

models.name: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B
models.desc: For a long stretch the best open model you could run locally for code.

models.name: Qwen2.5-VL-72B
models.desc: Open-weight vision at frontier quality, including document and GUI grounding.

models.name: Grok 4
models.desc: xAI's frontier reasoning model, with native search over X built into the loop.

models.name: Grok 4 Fast
models.desc: A two-million-token window at a twentieth of Grok 4's price.

models.name: Grok 3
models.desc: Trained on the Colossus cluster; the model that put xAI on the leaderboards.

models.name: Grok 3 Mini
models.desc: A cheap reasoning model with visible thinking traces.

models.name: Grok 2
models.desc: Released as open weights a year after launch.

models.name: Amazon Nova Premier
models.desc: The top of Amazon's own model line, built for distilling into smaller Novas.

models.name: Amazon Nova Pro
models.desc: Amazon's balanced multimodal model, priced aggressively inside Bedrock.

models.name: Amazon Nova Lite
models.desc: Very cheap multimodal inference with a 300k window.

models.name: Amazon Nova Micro
models.desc: Text-only and one of the cheapest models on any major cloud.

models.name: Phi-4
models.desc: 14B trained largely on synthetic curriculum data, and unusually strong at maths for its size.

models.name: Phi-4-reasoning-plus
models.desc: A 14B reasoning model distilled from o3-mini traces.

models.name: Phi-4-multimodal
models.desc: Text, vision and speech in 5.6B parameters, MIT-licensed.

models.name: Command A
models.desc: Runs on two GPUs, tuned for retrieval-augmented generation and 23 languages.

models.name: Command R+
models.desc: The model that made citation-grounded RAG a first-class API feature.

models.name: Command R7B
models.desc: Cohere's smallest — built for on-device RAG and tool use.

models.name: Jamba 1.6 Large
models.desc: A Mamba-Transformer hybrid — state-space layers keep long-context memory flat instead of quadratic.

models.name: Jamba 1.6 Mini
models.desc: 256k context on a single 80GB card, thanks to the hybrid architecture.

models.name: Kimi K3
models.desc: At 2.8 trillion parameters the largest open-weight model yet published — a multimodal mixture of experts routing 16 of 896 experts plus two shared ones per token, for 104B active. Weights released under a bespoke licence: open weights, not OSI open source.

models.name: Kimi K2 Thinking
models.desc: A trillion-parameter open-weight reasoning model that holds tool-use chains across hundreds of sequential calls.

models.name: Kimi K2 Instruct
models.desc: The first open-weight trillion-parameter model, trained with the Muon optimiser.

models.name: GLM-5.3
models.desc: Z.ai's flagship: 256 routed experts plus one shared, top-8 routing, about 39B active per token across a million-token window. Open weights under an MIT-style licence with one condition — a model-as-a-service operator above $10B revenue needs a Z.ai security review first.

models.name: GLM-4.6
models.desc: Widely used as an open drop-in for coding agents, with a 200k window.

models.name: GLM-4.5
models.desc: Unified reasoning, coding and agentic behaviour in one open MIT release.

models.name: GLM-4.5-Air
models.desc: A third the size of GLM-4.5 and close behind it — fits comfortably on one node.

models.name: MiniMax-M2
models.desc: Only 10B active parameters, which makes it unusually fast for its class on agentic workloads.

models.name: MiniMax-M1
models.desc: A million-token open-weight reasoning model using lightning attention.

models.name: Llama-3.1-Nemotron-Ultra-253B
models.desc: Llama 3.1 405B pruned to 253B by neural architecture search, then re-trained for reasoning.

models.name: Llama-3.3-Nemotron-Super-49B
models.desc: Distilled to fit a single H100 while keeping a reasoning toggle.

models.name: OLMo 2 32B
models.desc: Fully open: weights, data, code and training logs all published. The most reproducible model on this list.

models.name: Molmo 72B
models.desc: Trained without any distillation from closed models, and able to point at image regions.

models.name: Yi-Large
models.desc: 01.AI's bilingual flagship, and an early top-ten finish on LMArena for China.

models.name: Yi-1.5-34B
models.desc: A well-liked Apache-2.0 34B for bilingual work.

models.name: Reka Flash 3
models.desc: A 21B reasoning model with an explicit budget-forcing token to cap thinking length.

models.name: Reka Core
models.desc: One of the few models that ingests video and audio natively alongside text.

models.name: LFM2-8B-A1B
models.desc: A convolution-and-attention hybrid rather than a plain transformer, aimed at phones and embedded hardware.

models.name: Sonar Reasoning Pro
models.desc: A reasoning model wired directly to Perplexity's live web index, with citations in every answer.

models.name: Sonar Pro
models.desc: Search-grounded answers as an API primitive rather than a tool you assemble.

models.name: R1-1776
models.desc: DeepSeek-R1 post-trained to remove refusal patterns on politically sensitive topics, released openly.

models.name: ERNIE 4.5 300B-A47B
models.desc: Baidu's first open-weight release, with separate text and vision expert routing.

models.name: ERNIE X1
models.desc: Baidu's reasoning model, positioned against R1 at roughly half the price.

models.name: Hunyuan-A13B
models.desc: Fast and slow thinking modes in one model, at 13B active parameters.

models.name: Seed-OSS-36B
models.desc: A 512k-context open model with a thinking budget you set in tokens per request.

models.name: Step-3
models.desc: A multimodal MoE designed around decoding cost rather than parameter count.

models.name: Granite 3.3 8B
models.desc: Enterprise-focused, with published training-data provenance and an IP indemnity.

models.name: DBRX Instruct
models.desc: A fine-grained MoE with 16 experts, four active — an influential 2024 open release.

models.name: Solar Pro 2
models.desc: A Korean-first model that stays competitive in English at 31B.

models.name: Hermes 4 405B
models.desc: A steerable, minimally-filtered fine-tune of Llama 3.1 405B with hybrid reasoning.

models.name: Mercury Coder
models.desc: A diffusion language model rather than an autoregressive one — it denoises whole blocks of tokens at once, which is why it is so fast.

models.name: Claude Opus 5
models.desc: Anthropic's model for complex agentic coding and enterprise work, and the default recommendation for most workloads. Adaptive thinking is on by default and steered by an effort parameter rather than a token budget. Anthropic published no SWE-bench figure for it, leading instead on Frontier-Bench and CursorBench.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5
models.desc: The speed-and-intelligence tier of the Claude 5 family, and a drop-in upgrade from Sonnet 4.6. A million-token window at a fifth of Opus 5's price.

models.name: Claude Fable 5.1
models.desc: Anthropic's model for demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work — the one to reach for when Opus 5 at high effort still falls short. Thinking is always on and its raw chain of thought is never returned. Cache reads cost a quarter of what Fable 5 charged.

models.name: Claude Fable 5
models.desc: The first Fable model, now legacy and superseded by Fable 5.1 at the same input and output price. It introduced safety classifiers that decline requests with a refusal stop reason rather than an error, and server-side fallback to another model.

models.name: Claude Mythos 5.1
models.desc: Claude Fable 5.1's capabilities, specifications and pricing, offered by invitation only through Project Glasswing. Not generally available: access runs through Anthropic, AWS or Google Cloud account teams. It scores 60.9% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 against Fable 5.1's 55.8% on the same weights — Anthropic attributes the entire gap to Fable's safety classifiers intervening.

models.name: Claude Mythos 5
models.desc: Claude Fable 5's capabilities without its safety classifiers, released alongside it for defensive cybersecurity work under Project Glasswing. Same specifications and pricing as Fable 5; access is approved case by case.

models.name: GPT-4 Turbo
models.desc: The 2024 workhorse that first brought GPT-4 quality to a 128k window.

models.name: GPT-3.5 Turbo
models.desc: The model that started the commodity-LLM era. Kept here as a baseline.

models.name: o1-mini
models.desc: The first small reasoning model, focused on maths and code.

models.name: Gemini 2.0 Flash-Lite
models.desc: Google's cheapest tier of the 2.0 generation.

models.name: Gemini 1.5 Flash
models.desc: Distilled from 1.5 Pro; the first genuinely cheap million-token model.

models.name: Gemma 2 27B
models.desc: Punched well above its size in 2024 and stayed a common local default.

models.name: Gemma 2 9B
models.desc: Trained by distillation from a larger teacher rather than from scratch.

models.name: Llama 3.1 70B
models.desc: The mid-tier of the 3.1 family, superseded by 3.3 70B at the same size.

models.name: Llama 3.2 11B Vision
models.desc: The small end of Meta's open vision line.

models.name: Llama 3.2 1B
models.desc: Small enough to run on a phone CPU.

models.name: Qwen3-14B
models.desc: The largest Qwen3 that fits comfortably in 24GB with room for context.

models.name: Qwen3-8B
models.desc: Reasoning in 8B — the smallest size where the thinking switch still pays off.

models.name: Qwen3-4B
models.desc: Laptop-scale reasoning with a 128k window.

models.name: Qwen2.5-32B
models.desc: The Apache-2.0 32B that anchored a generation of local deployments.

models.name: Qwen2.5-7B
models.desc: One of the most widely fine-tuned small models in the open ecosystem.

models.name: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B
models.desc: R1's reasoning traces distilled into Qwen2.5-32B — the cheapest way to get R1-class maths locally.

models.name: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B
models.desc: Reasoning distilled all the way down to 8B.

models.name: DeepSeek-Coder-V2
models.desc: The first open code model to match GPT-4 Turbo on HumanEval.

models.name: Mistral NeMo 12B
models.desc: Built with NVIDIA; the Tekken tokenizer made it notably efficient on non-English text.

models.name: Mistral 7B
models.desc: The release that proved a small Apache-2.0 model could beat a much larger one, and set off the open fine-tuning boom.

models.name: Grok Code Fast 1
models.desc: Priced and tuned specifically for high-frequency agentic coding loops.

models.name: GLM-4-9B
models.desc: A strong bilingual 9B with long context, widely used in Chinese deployments.

models.name: Kimi-Dev-72B
models.desc: A 72B tuned purely for issue resolution — briefly the best open SWE-bench score.

models.name: Hunyuan-Large
models.desc: At release, the largest open transformer MoE published by anyone.

models.name: Nemotron Nano 9B v2
models.desc: A Mamba-Transformer hybrid with a reasoning budget you can cap per request.

models.name: OLMo 2 13B
models.desc: Fully open training data and code, at a size anyone can reproduce.

models.name: Phi-3.5-MoE
models.desc: 16 experts, two active — MIT-licensed and multilingual.

models.name: Falcon 3 10B
models.desc: Grown from a 7B by depth up-scaling rather than trained from scratch.

models.name: Falcon-H1 34B
models.desc: Runs attention and state-space layers in parallel rather than in sequence.

models.name: Falcon 180B
models.desc: The largest open model of 2023, and a marker of how fast the frontier moved.

models.name: xLAM-2-70B
models.desc: Trained specifically for multi-turn function calling rather than chat.

models.name: Snowflake Arctic
models.desc: 128 fine-grained experts, built for SQL and enterprise analytics rather than chat.

models.name: Palmyra X5
models.desc: A million-token enterprise model tuned for long-document workflows.

models.name: EXAONE 4.0 32B
models.desc: Korean-English bilingual with a unified reasoning and non-reasoning mode.

models.name: HyperCLOVA X SEED 14B
models.desc: Naver's open Korean-first release, trained largely on domestic data.

models.name: Sarvam-M
models.desc: A Mistral Small fine-tune for ten Indian languages, with a thinking mode.

models.name: Ling-1T
models.desc: A trillion-parameter open non-reasoning model from Ant Group's research arm.

models.name: MiniCPM4 8B
models.desc: Built around sparse attention for fast long-context inference on end devices.

models.name: dots.llm1
models.desc: Trained on 11.2T tokens with no synthetic data at all — an unusual choice, and the reason the release drew attention.

models.name: OpenELM 3B
models.desc: Apple's open research model, using layer-wise scaling to spend parameters where they matter most.

models.name: CorX3.8-27B
models.desc: Jamaica's first large open-weight LLM — a Jamaican Patois-speaking assistant fine-tuned from Qwen3.8-27B and fully merged.

models.name: TriStream-SVS
models.arch: 3 parallel encoders + late fusion trunk, rectified flow decoder
models.desc: A singing voice synthesis model that builds the source-filter theory of the human voice into its architecture as a hard constraint — pitch, timbre and breath texture run as three parallel encoder streams, combined only in a late fusion trunk. Generates at 24 kHz through rectified flow matching in roughly 32 sampling steps.

models.name: CorX1.5
models.desc: A 158M-parameter decoder-only transformer written and trained from scratch on a single GPU — architecture, tokenizer, pretraining and fine-tuning.
